messages:
IncidentBot: INCIDENT ALERT - High error rate detected on /v1/generate (errors ~18%) across US-east-1. Paging Oliver (on-call).

Oliver: got it, paging in. looking at logs now. any customer-facing impact confirmed?

Elaine: seeing increased 500s from the serving runtime, looks like a KV cache eviction surge after a deploy at 16:12 UTC. Affects hosted API only.

Samir: reported from one large customer (acme-corp) with degraded generation latency, they filed a ticket. Samir on standby for comms.

Oliver: doing quick mitigation — scaling up burst pool and enabling fallback model variant. will update status page after mitigation results.

IncidentBot: On-call handover: Oliver accepted at 1763205140. Previous oncall: Elaine.

Elaine: handing off now — logs + repro in #eng-runtime. TL;DR: a runtime change introduced more frequent KV invalidations under certain sequence-length distributions. patch incoming.

Maria: @PressOps @Legal heads-up — we'll need public wording for status page + possible tweet/blog. Do not post until we agree on messaging and status page reflects correct scope.

PressOps: thanks. priority is: 1) status page accurate 2) short customer notification 3) social post only if incident has material customer impact or wide visibility.

Legal: quick note — avoid implying data loss, avoid committing timelines for RC until triage complete. Keep wording factual.

Samir: draft customer email (for affected customers) below:

```
Subject: Service degradation affecting /v1/generate — temporary increased errors
Hi <Customer>,
We detected an increase in error rates for the hosted generation endpoint starting at 16:12 UTC. Our engineers are investigating and have applied mitigations to reduce impact. You may see intermittent 500 responses; persistence should be low. We’ll provide updates on our status page: https://status.redwood.ai/ and follow up when resolved.
Apologies for the disruption — Samir, Support
```

Maria: thanks Samir — please don't send to customers yet. We need to agree on the public short message first. Proposing two options for external channels (tweet-length and longer blog snippet).

Maria: OPTION A (short, conservative):
"We are investigating an increased error rate affecting the hosted text generation API in US-east. Our engineers have deployed mitigations and are monitoring. Status: https://status.redwood.ai/"

Maria: OPTION B (slightly more detailed):
"We’re investigating an uptick in errors for our hosted text generation endpoint in US-east caused by a runtime cache invalidation issue. We're rolling mitigations and will post updates to https://status.redwood.ai/. We’ll follow up with a root-cause once confirmed."

PressOps: both look good. prefer A for social -> shorter. For blog/update page we can use B with a follow-up once RCA is ready.

Legal: prefer B but remove phrase "cache invalidation" in public social until we confirm cause; keep that in the status page as engineering detail. Suggest social:
"We’re investigating an uptick in errors for our hosted text generation endpoint in US-east. Engineers have applied mitigations and are monitoring. More at https://status.redwood.ai/"

Oliver: mitigation scaled burst pool + fallback model, error rate dropped to ~3% at 1763205325. Root cause seems tied to the runtime deploy earlier — digging into a revert/patch now.

Maria: OK, we have consensus on social wording from Legal. PressOps: can you queue the tweet but do not publish until status page is set to "identified"? Need the status page to reflect "investigating" -> "identified" -> "monitoring/resolved" progression to avoid confusion.

PressOps: ack. drafting tweet now and will wait for status page update. Draft below (ready for publish once status page shows identified):

"We’re investigating an uptick in errors for our hosted text generation endpoint in US-east. Engineers have applied mitigations and are monitoring. More at https://status.redwood.ai/"

Elaine: creating a short status page update now. Proposed status timeline entry:
- 16:12 UTC: Errors increase observed
- 16:18 UTC: Mitigations applied (burst capacity + fallback model)
- 16:28 UTC: Error rate reduced, monitoring

IncidentBot: status update posted draft to https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1763205123-draft (internal).

Samir: once status page shows "identified" I'll prepare the customer-facing email (finalize with PR). Also will prepare a template for account execs to send to high-touch customers.

Maria: small ask — can we include a one-line blog follow-up after RCA? e.g., "We resolved an issue related to the runtime caching strategy after a recent deploy; full RCA to follow." Keep it non-technical for marketing.

Oliver: plan: revert the recent runtime patch in canary, run regression tests, then canary release. If green, roll to prod. ETA for patch/revert 30-45 mins.

PressOps: timeline noted. We'll hold social until status progression is visible. After RCA, we'll post a blog snippet similar to Maria's suggested line and link to detailed engineering post.

Legal: approve the short public message as-is. Please avoid naming customers or specific latency numbers in social.

Maria: final checklist before publish:
- [ ] Status page updated to "identified" and contains mitigation timeline (Elaine)
- [ ] Incident severity & customer impact confirmed (Samir + Oliver)
- [ ] Tweet drafted & queued (PressOps)
- [ ] Customer email template approved (Samir + Maria)
- [ ] Legal sign-off on wording (Legal)

Oliver: updating status page to "identified" at 1763205380. patch revert in canary underway.

IncidentBot: Handoff note: Oliver remains on-call. Next check-in scheduled 1763205600.

PressOps: status page now shows "identified". publishing queue unlocked — publishing tweet in ~2 mins. posting update to status page to reflect monitoring once patch validated.

Maria: thanks team — good coordination. after the tweet goes out, I'll send the customer email to the approved list and push a short blog placeholder that will link to the engineering RCA once ready.

Samir: sending account exec template to private channel for high-touch customers.

Oliver: closing loop — error rate stable ~1.5% after canary revert. will continue monitoring and file RCA.

PressOps: tweet published (1763205398). link: https://twitter.com/redwood/status/xxxxx (internal placeholder).

Maria: social posted. monitoring replies. I'll coordinate follow-up blog with engineering write-up.

Legal: thanks — keeping this one low-key was wise.

Elaine: I'll prepare the engineering post and attach logs, PR diff, and timeline. expected RCA draft in ~24 hours.

Oliver: thanks everyone. moving to post-incident notes and follow-ups.

Samir: will close customer tickets with note and link to status page and follow-up RCA when available.

PressOps: adding final note for records: do not amplify on Mastodon until blog/engineering post published.

IncidentBot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, status: monitoring.
